line: I’m smokin’ dope, I get so high, I meet my demons (I do)
vault_lines: I'm smokin' dope, I get so high, I meet my demons (I do)
meaning:
Smoking dope, a slang term for marijuana, is an activity LAROI often partakes in as expressed throughout his discography. A prime example of this is in his appearance on Internet Money’s August 2020 track “Speak,” where he drops multiple bars on the topic:

I’m ‘bout to get high, pass me the spliff, bitch, I'ma face it (Oh, oh)
…
Uh, smoking on that green (Oh yeah), hell nah, oh, please

However, LAROI’s use of marijuana only first became evident in 2020, and in fact, he seemingly used to stay away from the drug altogether. In an August 2019 No Jumper video, channel creator adam22 touched on the subject:

So for the record, The Kid LAROI does not smoke weed

line: Bought my mom a crib, fuck designer, I do not know Raf
vault_lines: Bought my mom a crib, fuck designer, I do not know Raf
meaning:
LAROI sets his priorities straight, opting to purchase a house for his mom rather than buying designer clothing, namely that of Belgian fashion designer Raf Simons. This is not the first time LAROI has mentioned this purchase in his lyrics, as he dropped a similar line in his November 2020 track “PIKACHU”:

This year I bought my mom a house, who would’ve knew that I would

In a Genius Verified annotation on his December 2019 breakout hit “Let Her Go,” LAROI expands on the purchase:

I just was able to pay off our house for my mom in Los Angeles. I moved to Los Angeles. I wanted to do that ever since I was younger. And all of these things that I dreamt of when I was younger is starting to finally come true.

Ironically, in “Let Her Go,” LAROI also mentions purchasing Raf Simons clothing:

New Rick, new Raf, fuck about a hater, homie

line: Just turned seventeen, the shit I’ve seen, they wouldn’t believe it (They wouldn’t)
vault_lines: Just turned seventeen, the shit I've seen, they wouldn't believe it (They wouldn't)
meaning:
LAROI acknowledges his 17th birthday, which occurred on August 17, 2020, around the same time this song was recorded and previewed.

LAROI also notes his mature experiences, a theme he touched on in his July 2020 single, “TELL ME WHY,” where he pays homage to the family and friends he lost:

I seen shit, I’m way too damn young, it shouldn’t need to be like this

line: Now I’m in L.A. eating sushi next to The Weeknd (Huh)
vault_lines: Now I'm in L.A. eating sushi next to The Weeknd (Huh)
meaning:
LAROI goes over his newly-found fame by remarking his location, Los Angeles, a popular place for celebrities to reside in. LAROI namedrops The Weeknd, another budding artist who spiraled to fame with popularized albums, such as November 2016’s Starboy and March 2020’s After Hours. The Weeknd is currently settled in Hidden Hills with a $25 Million dollar mansion.

LAROI touches more on his fame in “PIKACHU,” a solo track from F*CK LOVE (SAVAGE) where he swiftly raps about his evolution from a poor to rich kid:

I used to pray for some better days
Ten years later, I’m in L.A. whippin' a Bentayga

line: M.O.B., fuck all these bitches, I’m focused on gettin’ paid
vault_lines: M.O.B., fuck all these bitches, I'm focused on gettin' paid
meaning:
“M.O.B.” is an acronym popularized by the late rap icon 2Pac from his March 2001 track of the same name, standing for “money over bitches.” As the phrase emphasizes girls only wanting men for their fame, it has been commonly used throughout the rap scene.

LAROI says similar lines elsewhere on F*CK LOVE 3: OVER YOU, specifically on “OVER YOU,” where he raps:

M.O.B., money over sex and I D-I-E when I need my checks

line: I’m with big bro Swerv’, bumping Juice WRLD, that no issue
vault_lines: I'm with big bro Swerv', bumping Juice WRLD, that no issue
meaning:
LAROI references G Herbo’s nickname “Swervo,“ or “Swerv',“ which came about through Herbo’s July 2018 album Swervo and the album’s titular track.

He also name drops his late mentor and good friend Juice WRLD, who tragically passed away on December 8, 2019 due to an accidental overdose of oxycodone and codeine.

LAROI further alludes to Juice and Future’s October 2018 track “No Issue,” on which the pair rap about their lifestyle with fame and drugs.

One day prior to their collaborative June 2020 hit “GO,“ LAROI explained the significance Juice had on his life and paying homage to the singer:

it’s been a little over 6 months since you been gone, and it still doesn’t feel right. before we even met you were my favourite artist, and I still think everyday how cool it was that I got to b damn near family with my idol. you took me all over the world on a f*cking private jet and showed me a whole different side of life that not many people get to see. from all the months you let me live at your crib, to all the nights I spent watching and learning from you in the studio, to all the concerts and tours I got to witness.. I got to learn from a real life legend. it’s not even in my character to write long ass shit like this but fuck it our song is about to come out and I just wanna say how much I wish you were here with me to enjoy this shit. we all love and miss you back here ❤️

line: Just two years ago, my mama was off the drugs, tweakin’
vault_lines: Just two years ago, my mama was off the drugs, tweakin'
meaning:
Before achieving fame, LAROI and his family used to live homeless in Australia. LAROI explained in his Spotify RADAR Documentary:

Me and my family didn’t have a house and shit like that. But then it got to a point, you know, where we had nowhere to go. […] And bro was, like, literally cooking meth, like, right next to us. Shit was getting really hectic. I had to watch my mom do a lot of shit to survive and keep us, like, fed and shit.

line: I wake up and I thank God, I done been through it all
vault_lines: I wake up and I thank God, I done been through it all
meaning:
LAROI directly recalls lyrics from another unreleased track, “Betty Crock,” which contrary to his melodious style, is developed in a rap fashion. Throughout the song, LAROI discusses his dangerous and risky lifestyle:

Every day, I thank the lord, cuz' I done been through a lot

line: How the fuck I’m in this crib? I was sleepin’ on floors
vault_lines: How the fuck I'm in this crib? I was sleepin' on floors
meaning:
LAROI describes his homeless lifestyle before he found fame, explained in his Spotify RADAR Documentary:

Me and my family didn’t have a house and shit like that. But then it got to a point, you know, where we had nowhere to go. We were, like, staying on my mom’s friend’s couch and shit like that.

LAROI has incorporated his experiences into the first track off of the Deluxe project to his debut mixtape F*CK LOVE, “PIKACHU:”

Ninth grade, dropped out of school, used to sleep on JD’s couch

line: Saw my uncle in the grave, when my heart turn cold
vault_lines: Saw my uncle in the grave, when my heart turn cold
meaning:
In a June 2020 tweet, LAROI explained that his uncle was murdered when he was younger, and later touched on his influence in an interview with Sidedoor:

In the early stages of my life, my dad was always in an out, so my uncle was a really big male figure in my life. When he got murdered, it just made me really want to do it. ‘Cause he would always tell me, “stick to rapping, don’t ever do no dumb shit, don’t become like me, don’t do the things that I do, I want you to stick to rapping,“ so I was like, “Damn, I wanna take it seriously now.“ That was the main thing that fueled me at 10 [years old.]
